outcome: Current supported decision retained; new future-regime caveat.
criticalFinding: September publication does not mean commencement: the Act and Regulations take effect on 1 November2026.

provisions: 1997 Act sections2-4 cover the defined plant class and permissions. Definition does not expressly include all manufactured plant products.

The currently published authority FAQ specifically allows processed tea commercially packaged, with declaration and arrival inspection. Web placement is Import/Export rather than Travel; PDF page4 has the same tea answer.
The department link labeled 2014 revision is actually Amendment Law13of2014. Its changes concern institutional names and live/viable alien plants, not a new manufactured-tea definition.

cites: Reg2 and Schedule1 p10 list other regulated articles, none specifically tea
Reg4(b) requires business licence only where permit is used for trade/business
Schedule2 p11-12 is a fee table, not an exhaustive plant-product exemption list
regulations.finding: No tea-specific rule or personal postal waiver appears. Its absence alone does not establish future permission.

cites: Section2 p9: living plant category; unmanufactured materials and manufactured products capable of pest risk are plant products
Section3 p10: other regulated article definition requires pest capacity and regulatory prescription
Sections15-16 pp12-13: covered imports require permit and phytosanitary certificate, subject to Director exemption powers
Section53 p29: 1997 Act repeal and savings for existing permits/certificates
act.finding: Manufactured tea is not automatically included merely because derived from leaves. Nor is the statute itself a categorical processed-tea exemption. Existing authority tea guidance supports the current decision; no firm future-regime classification recovered.

scopeInference: The current specific processed-tea guidance is unqualified as to mode; postal scope follows from that general commodity guidance, not from a baggage exemption.
futureQuestion: Whether existing packaged-tea allowance continues as classification or exemption under new Act from1November. No bespoke ruling inherently needed if the authority publishes generally applicable guidance.
